title: Enterprise Voice Funnel: SLA-triggered Prioritization & Roadmap Lane Mapping
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Create a repeatable, measurable intake funnel that turns high-priority customer voice (top accounts and escalations) into deterministic roadmap actions. The funnel will: capture signals (support tickets, account exec escalations, CSM notes, NPS rumbles, incident postmortems), score requests with a transparent SLA-triggering algorithm, map resulting work to explicit roadmap lanes (Urgent Fix / Dedicated Capacity / High-Impact Feature / Research), and surface actionable items to PM/Eng/design triage within defined SLAs. Goal: reduce time-to-decision for top-account asks from weeks to <72 hours and ensure predictable routing into cycles or hotfix flows.
acceptance_criteria: A documented intake schema capturing 8 signal sources and normalized fields (ARR, affected-users, severity, security/regulatory flag, data-sensitivity)
A triage scoring formula implemented in the intake sheet/dashboard that outputs a numeric priority and SLA tier
Automated alerting when SLA tier breaches (initial response <=4h for P0 customers), routed to on-call PM/Eng/SE
Mapping rules that assign items to one of 4 roadmap lanes and suggest cycle assignment (canary, next cycle, deferred)
Runbook + stakeholder RACI for escalations that includes expected compensatory actions (billing credits, config changes, temporary service adjustments)
Pilot ingestion of 10 historical escalations and validation that the funnel reproduces prior routing decisions with >=80% match to human triage
success_metrics: Median time from escalation to roadmap decision <=72 hours
% of top-account asks with clear owner assigned within SLA >=90%
Reduction in ad-hoc executive escalations by 40% after pilot
Number of critical regressions handled via Dedicated lane with no customer downtime >=95% compliance to runbook
proposed_flow: 1) Ingest signals via web form + slack channel + support integration + AE intake. 2) Normalize to intake schema and compute triage score (weighted factors: ARR 30%, severity 25%, regulatory 20%, repeat-occurrence 15%, strategic-fit 10%). 3) Assign SLA tier (P0 immediate, P1 72h, P2 next cycle). 4) Automated routing: P0 -> hotfix/hotlane + on-call PM, P1 -> prioritized lane w/ assigned owner, P2 -> backlog funnel. 5) Weekly review for P1/P2 items slated for cycle commit.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Discovery, 2 weeks): interview 12 AEs/CSMs, analyze 24 historical escalations, validate scoring weights
Phase 1 (Prototype, 3 weeks): build intake sheet + Slack intake + triage dashboard; run closed pilot with 5 accounts
Phase 2 (Pilot, 4 weeks): onboard 25 top accounts, tune thresholds, add automated alerting to PagerDuty/Slack
Phase 3 (Ship, 2 weeks): embed mapping into roadmap tooling, train PMs/CS/Eng, publish runbook
Phase 4 (Operationalize): handoff to Support Ops, define quarterly review cadence and OKR linkage
risks: Scoring algorithm may over-index ARR and miss high-severity low-ARR regulatory issues
Insufficient engineering capacity to honor P0 hotfix SLA leading to degraded trust
Data quality gaps in historical tickets could bias weight tuning
Manual steps (CS intake) create bottlenecks unless automated integrations are implemented
